notYet: Not yet part of Athens and the Aegean

stages.name: Outside the war
stages.desc: Kingdoms, leagues and cities that stay out of the Athenian–Spartan struggle

stages.name: Athens
stages.desc: Attica, the city-state of Socrates, ruled by its citizens' Assembly

stages.name: Athens' empire and allies
stages.desc: Members of the Delian League, paying tribute to Athens

stages.name: Sparta and its allies
stages.desc: Sparta, the Peloponnesian League and the Boeotians

stages.name: Revolt and battle
stages.desc: Cities in revolt against Athens, or fought over

stages.name: Sparta's rule
stages.desc: After 404: Spartan governors and garrisons, and the Thirty in Athens

states.name: West Macedonia
timeline: The upland principalities of Macedonia

states.name: Epirus
timeline: The Molossians and other peoples of Epirus; the oracle of Dodona

states.name: Centre Macedonia
timeline: The Greek cities of Chalcidice pay tribute to Athens; Macedon's kings rule inland
Potidaea revolts; Socrates serves in the two-year siege
Potidaea surrenders and is resettled by Athenians
The Spartan Brasidas wins over the Chalcidian cities
Sparta takes over Athens' former allies in the north

states.name: East Macedonia and Thrace
timeline: Thasos and the Thracian coast, rich in silver and timber
Thasos revolts over its mines and is besieged for two years
Thasos surrenders its fleet and its mainland mines
Athens founds Amphipolis on the Strymon river
Brasidas takes Amphipolis; the historian Thucydides is exiled for failing to save it
Battle of Amphipolis: Brasidas and Cleon both die; Socrates serves there
Sparta takes over Athens' former allies in the north

states.name: Mount Athos
timeline: The cities of the Athos peninsula, tribute payers to Athens
Brasidas campaigns on the peninsula
Sparta takes over Athens' former allies in the north

states.name: Thessalia
timeline: Thessaly's horse-breeding aristocracies, allied to Athens on paper from 461

states.name: Central Greece
timeline: Boeotia under Thebes, Phocis with Delphi, and Euboea
After the battle of Oenophyta, Athens dominates Boeotia and Phocis
The Boeotians defeat Athens at Coronea; Boeotia will fight on Sparta's side
The Boeotians rout the Athenians at Delium; Socrates is in the retreat
Thebes, though Sparta's ally, shelters Athenian exiles from the Thirty

states.name: Attica
timeline: Athens leads the Greek alliance against Persia; Socrates is born at Alopeke, outside the walls
The Long Walls are finished, joining the city to its harbour at Piraeus
War with Sparta: the country people crowd inside the walls
Plague: tens of thousands die in the crowded city
Sparta fortifies Decelea, in Attica itself, and holds it for the rest of the war
Athens surrenders; the Thirty rule with a Spartan garrison on the Acropolis
The democrats return from Piraeus; democracy and an amnesty are restored
Socrates is tried, condemned and put to death

states.name: Peloponnese
timeline: Sparta and its Peloponnesian League; Corinth and Argos are the other great cities
Spartan armies march out to ravage Attica almost every summer

states.name: West Greece
timeline: Achaea, Elis, Aetolia and Acarnania
Athens settles Messenian rebels from Sparta at Naupactus
Phormio's Athenian squadron defeats larger Peloponnesian fleets off Naupactus
With Athens' defeat, Sparta's side prevails; the Messenians are soon driven from Naupactus

states.name: Crete
timeline: The cities of Crete stay outside the great alliances

states.name: South Aegean
timeline: The Cyclades and the islands off Asia Minor, tribute-paying members of the Delian League
Neutral Melos refuses to submit; Athens kills its men and enslaves its women and children
Rhodes and other islands go over to Sparta
Lysander sets Spartan governors and pro-Spartan boards over the islands

states.name: North Aegean
timeline: Lesbos, Chios, Samos and Lemnos: Athens' strongest allies, with fleets of their own
Mytilene on Lesbos revolts; Athens nearly orders the whole male population killed
Mytilene surrenders and Lesbos is divided among Athenian settlers
Chios revolts after the Sicilian disaster; Samos becomes the Athenian fleet's base
Athens wins the great sea battle of Arginusae, off Lesbos
Samos, last loyal ally, falls to Lysander

states.name: Ionian Islands
timeline: Corcyra, a strong naval power, keeps out of the alliances
Corcyra allies with Athens against Corinth, one of the sparks of the war
Civil war on Corcyra between democrats and oligarchs (Thucydides)
The democrats win and Corcyra stays with Athens
Corcyra stays outside Sparta's new order

events.title: Born at Alopeke
events.text: Socrates, son of the stoneworker Sophroniscus and the midwife Phaenarete, is born just outside the walls (c. 470/469).

events.title: Thasos revolts
events.text: The island of Thasos rebels against Athens over its gold and silver mines and is besieged for two years.

events.title: Ephialtes' reforms
events.text: The old council of the Areopagus loses its powers; the Assembly and the people's courts now rule Athens.

events.title: The Long Walls
events.text: Two walls, each about six kilometres long, now join Athens to its harbour at Piraeus.

events.title: Oenophyta
events.text: Athens defeats the Boeotians and dominates central Greece for ten years.

events.title: Treasury to Athens
events.text: The Delian League's treasury is moved from Delos to Athens: the alliance has become an empire.

events.title: Anaxagoras' book
events.text: In Plato's Phaedo, the young Socrates hears a reading from Anaxagoras, who taught that Mind orders all things (c. 450).

events.title: Parthenon begun
events.text: Work starts on the Parthenon; it is finished in 432, paid for partly with the allies' tribute.

events.title: Coronea
events.text: The Boeotians defeat Athens and win back their freedom.

events.title: The oracle's answer
events.text: At an unknown date, Chaerephon asks Delphi whether anyone is wiser than Socrates. The answer: no one.

events.title: Amphipolis founded
events.text: Athens founds a colony on the Strymon to control Thracian timber and gold.

events.title: Corcyra allies with Athens
events.text: Athens backs Corcyra against Corinth: one of the quarrels that start the great war.

events.title: Siege of Potidaea
events.text: Socrates serves as a hoplite; Plato says he saved the wounded Alcibiades and walked barefoot on the ice.

events.title: The war begins
events.text: Sparta invades Attica; Pericles brings the country people inside the walls and honours the first dead.

events.title: The plague
events.text: Plague breaks out in Piraeus and sweeps the crowded city; a mass grave of its victims was found in 1994–95.

events.title: Pericles dies
events.text: Athens' leading statesman dies of the plague.

events.title: Phormio's victories
events.text: A small Athenian squadron beats two larger Peloponnesian fleets in the Corinthian Gulf.

events.title: Mytilene revolts
events.text: Lesbos rebels; the Assembly orders all its men killed, then sends a second ship to stop the massacre.

events.title: Civil war on Corcyra
events.text: Democrats and oligarchs slaughter each other; Thucydides makes it a portrait of war's cruelty.

events.title: Delium
events.text: The Boeotians rout the Athenians; Plato and Laches praise Socrates' calm in the retreat.

events.title: Brasidas takes Amphipolis
events.text: Sparta's boldest general wins Athens' Thracian colony.

events.title: The Clouds
events.text: Aristophanes puts Socrates on stage in a basket, running a school of clever nonsense. It comes third.

events.title: Battle of Amphipolis
events.text: Socrates' third campaign; both Brasidas and the Athenian leader Cleon are killed.

events.title: Peace of Nicias
events.text: Athens and Sparta make a fifty-year peace; within eight years they are openly at war again.

events.title: Melos
events.text: Athens conquers neutral Melos, kills its men and enslaves its women and children.

events.title: The fleet sails for Sicily
events.text: A great armada leaves Piraeus; two years later it is destroyed at Syracuse.

events.title: The herms smashed
events.text: The stone figures of Hermes at the city's doorways are mutilated in one night; the city hunts for traitors.

events.title: Decelea
events.text: Sparta fortifies a base in Attica itself; Athens' farms and silver mines are lost.

events.title: Chios revolts
events.text: After the Sicilian disaster, Athens' richest allies begin to defect.

events.title: The Four Hundred
events.text: An oligarchy seizes Athens for four months before the democracy returns.

events.title: Arginusae
events.text: Athens wins its last great sea battle, but storms keep the crews of sinking ships from being rescued.

events.title: Socrates says no
events.text: The Assembly tries the generals together, illegally. Socrates, on the presiding committee by lot, refuses to agree.

events.title: Aegospotami
events.text: Lysander captures the Athenian fleet on its beach in the Hellespont; Athens is starved into surrender.

events.title: The walls come down
events.text: Athens surrenders; the Long Walls are pulled down to the music of pipe-girls, says Xenophon.

events.title: Leon of Salamis
events.text: The Thirty, led by Critias, order Socrates to arrest an innocent man. He goes home instead.

events.title: Lysander's new order
events.text: Sparta's admiral sets governors and pro-Spartan boards of ten over Athens' former allies.

events.title: Phyle
events.text: Thrasybulus and some seventy exiles seize a border fort and begin the fight back.

events.title: Munichia
events.text: The democrats beat the Thirty on the hill above Piraeus; Critias is killed. An amnesty follows.

events.title: The charge
events.text: At the King's Stoa, Meletus charges Socrates with not recognising the city's gods, bringing in new ones, and corrupting the young.

events.title: The verdict
events.text: About five hundred citizen jurors find him guilty, by about 280 to 220, and then choose death.

events.title: The sacred ship
events.text: No execution may take place while the state ship is on its yearly voyage to Delos; Socrates waits about a month.

events.title: Death in prison
events.text: Socrates drinks the poison in the state prison, perhaps the building found south-west of the Agora.

events.title: Refuge at Megara
events.text: Plato and other companions withdraw for a time to Megara, says Diogenes Laertius.

chartNote: Share of the area of modern Greece, by the alignment of each present-day region's leading cities in the struggle between Athens and Sparta. Regions are today's boundaries and often mixed (Boeotia and Euboea share one region), and the islands' allies on the coast of Asia Minor are not counted. A simplification; dates are approximate turning points.
